chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise, I bear witness that there is no god but You, I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Kun Fayakun' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this verse within the doctrine of *Kun Fayakun* ('Be, and it is'), emphasizing Allah’s absolute sovereignty and the immediacy of His creative command without intermediary causes. This concept is central to Shia theological discussions on divine omnipotence and is often linked to the Prophet’s declaration of his own status as the 'Word' of Allah, reinforcing the link between divine speech and creation.
